suggested_experiment_name: Gamma-ray attenuation (EBL optical depth, Fermi-LAT + IACT blazars)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (plot shows log10(g_agamma/GeV^-1); values converted from log10 axis readings)
notes: Paper sets bounds on ALP-photon coupling g_agamma over 8-25 eV mass range from gamma-ray optical depth (EBL attenuation) using Fermi-LAT + Cherenkov blazar data. No numerical table provided; exclusion is presented in Fig. 3 contours (log10(g_agamma/GeV^-1) from -14 to -9 vs log10(m_a c^2/eV) from -0.2 to 1.6). Data points above are approximate estimates reconstructed from the text: best fit m_a c^2 = 9.1 eV, Gamma_a = 2.5e-24 s^-1 (g = 2.1e-11 GeV^-1) at only 2.1-sigma preference, interpreted by authors as an upper bound; limit scales roughly as g ~ m^-3/2 for a roughly constant Gamma_a limit. Assumes ALPs are ALL of cosmological dark matter (Omega_a * rho_c), not a local halo density assumption. Bounds are cosmological/astrophysical, improving prior limits (MUSE, VIMOS, globular clusters) by up to an order of magnitude in this range.
